## How they got there
Liverpool reached the final as runners-up after losing to Real Madrid 0-1, a journey propelled by their dominance in key offensive metrics where they outperformed the vast majority of their peers. The team beat more teams than any other on Points per game at 97% and Attacks per game at 84%, while also ranking highly in Passes per game (78%) and Shot accuracy (97%). These figures placed them among the most prolific attacking sides in the competition's history, with their 57.5 attacks per game surpassing 93% of all Champions League teams since 2011-12.

## Would the model have picked them?
The model assigned Liverpool a 32.5% probability of reaching the final, significantly higher than the 12.5% base rate for a random knockout team, and ranked them second among all participants in that season. Because only two teams reach each final, this top-two rank confirms the model would have selected them as a primary candidate rather than just a leading contender. Their expected stage figure of 2.24 sits nearest to the semi-finals on the scale where zero represents elimination before the quarter-finals and three indicates losing the final.

## Weak spots
In terms of league performance, Liverpool beat fewer teams than others in Distance covered per game (25%), Long passes (% of passes) at 47%, and Fouls committed per game (38%). While the model marked down their foul rate as a negative factor, they still ranked better than only 38% of that season's teams on this metric. Additionally, although the model assigned a negative contribution to Opponent shots on target per game, Liverpool actually performed well by beating 86% of teams in that category.

messages.content: You are a football performance analyst writing for a curious, data-literate reader. Use ONLY the facts provided. Quote every number exactly as it appears in the facts, with the same rounding. Do not introduce players, managers, matches, events, analyses or numbers that are not in the facts. 'Better than this %' figures say how many teams the club beat on a stat, so higher is always better, including for stats marked '(lower is better)', where beating a team means having the lower value. SHAP contributions are measured in knockout stages: a positive contribution means the stat pushed the model's expected stage up by that fraction of a round, a negative one pushed it down. A SHAP contribution is the model's view, not a measure of how good the team was at the stat: a team can rank high on a stat the model marked down, so never call a stat a strength or a weakness because of its SHAP sign. Everything here is a statistical association, not a cause: never say a stat drove, propelled, hindered or prevented a result, and do not explain why a stat got its contribution. Write plain markdown without tables.
